title: Read a platform letter
description: Read the platform or track mark on a sign and say which train side it names.
oneStarDescription: Point to the letter or number.
twoStarDescription: Say whether it names a platform, a track, or a car, from the words beside it.
threeStarDescription: If the sign does not say, write that you would ask.

title: Read a postage mark
description: Read a stamp or a printed postage mark and say what it does not tell you.
oneStarDescription: Point to the postage mark and not to the picture beside it.
twoStarDescription: Read one word or value you can see.
threeStarDescription: Say one thing it does not tell you, such as the date it was posted if that is missing.

title: Read a queue ticket
description: Read a queue number and say how you will know when it is your turn.
oneStarDescription: Read the number on the ticket.
twoStarDescription: Point to the display or the board that calls numbers.
threeStarDescription: Say how many numbers are between the display and yours, or that you cannot see the display.

title: Read a clock with Roman numerals
description: Read the hour on a clock face that uses Roman numerals.
oneStarDescription: Point to the shorter hand.
twoStarDescription: Say the numeral it has passed.
threeStarDescription: Say the hour in ordinary words.

title: Read a Roman numeral date
description: Read a year written in Roman numerals and write it in ordinary digits.
oneStarDescription: Point to each numeral you know.
twoStarDescription: Write the year in digits.
threeStarDescription: Point to a pair such as IV or IX and say what it does, or say the date has none.

title: Read the digits under a barcode
description: Read the digits printed under a barcode and find them again on a second look.
oneStarDescription: Read the digits aloud. Another person can confirm, from what they see or hear, that you can read the digits.
twoStarDescription: Look away and write them.
threeStarDescription: Check against the package and mark a wrong digit.

title: Read one braille cell
description: Learn one braille cell from a reference and find it again by touch or by sight.
oneStarDescription: Match one letter to its dot pattern from a reference.
twoStarDescription: Find that pattern among three you can see or feel.
threeStarDescription: Say that one cell is not reading.

title: Read one tab number
description: Point to one number on a tab staff and press that fret on the string it names.
oneStarDescription: Point to one written number.
twoStarDescription: Say which line of the tab it sits on.
threeStarDescription: Press that fret, or say the diagram does not match your instrument.

title: Read opposite faces on a die
description: Say which faces are opposite on a standard die you can check.
oneStarDescription: Name one pair of opposite faces.
twoStarDescription: Look at the die and say whether that pair is opposite.
threeStarDescription: From a face you see, say the hidden opposite.

title: Referee a coin flip
description: Flip a coin where both people can see it, and call the result only after it lands.
oneStarDescription: Show both faces before the flip.
twoStarDescription: Let it land on a surface, not on a hand you cover.
threeStarDescription: Call the face only after it has landed, and show it.

title: Reject a net that will not fold
description: Look at two cube nets and say which one will not fold into a closed cube, then test with paper.
oneStarDescription: Point to the net you think will fail.
twoStarDescription: Fold both, or fold the one you rejected.
threeStarDescription: Say whether your choice was right.

title: Reveal a lemon line with a lamp
description: Write with lemon juice, let it dry, and warm it with a lamp until the line shows or you stop.
oneStarDescription: Write one line and let it dry.
twoStarDescription: Hold the paper near a lamp, not a flame, and watch.
threeStarDescription: Stop when the line shows or when the paper smells hot, and say which.

title: Roll a cloth strip
description: Roll a cloth strip into a tight roll that stays when you set it down.
oneStarDescription: Start a tight end that stays tight when you pinch it.
twoStarDescription: Roll the strip. Another person can confirm, from what they see or hear, that you can roll it.
threeStarDescription: Set it down and say whether it unrolled.

title: Roll a coin across your knuckles
description: Roll a coin across the knuckles of one hand so a watcher can see it travel.
oneStarDescription: Roll the coin from one knuckle to the next without dropping it.
twoStarDescription: Roll it across the row and catch it in the same hand.
threeStarDescription: Do it once while someone watches, and pick it up if it falls.

title: Roll a hoop and catch it
description: Roll a hoop in a straight line and catch it before it falls.
oneStarDescription: Roll the hoop so it stays up.
twoStarDescription: Catch it while it is still upright.
threeStarDescription: Say whether it rolled straight.

title: Roll a pencil and catch it
description: Roll a pencil down your forearm and catch it in that hand.
oneStarDescription: Set the pencil on the forearm and let it start.
twoStarDescription: Catch the pencil before it hits the floor.
threeStarDescription: Show the pencil in the hand after the catch.

title: Roll a tie for a bag
description: Roll a necktie so it does not crease into a hard fold, and unroll it.
oneStarDescription: Roll from the narrow end.
twoStarDescription: Put it in a bag and take it out.
threeStarDescription: Unroll it and say whether a hard crease appeared.

title: Roll a towel for a bag
description: Roll a towel tightly enough that it stays rolled in a bag.
oneStarDescription: Roll the towel from one end.
twoStarDescription: Put it in a bag and take it out.
threeStarDescription: Say whether it stayed rolled.

title: Run a cord through a casing
description: Run a cord through a fabric or paper channel and show both ends.
oneStarDescription: Use a folded channel you can open at the ends.
twoStarDescription: Push or pull the cord through.
threeStarDescription: Show an end sticking out of each side.

title: Run a short domino line
description: Stand a short line of dominoes so tipping the first tips the last.
oneStarDescription: Stand at least six dominoes with a gap you chose.
twoStarDescription: Tip the first and show the last fell, or say where it stopped.
threeStarDescription: Reset the gap that failed and run that part again.

title: Say a tongue twister cleanly
description: Say a short tongue twister through once without a stumble you ignore.
oneStarDescription: Say it once at a pace you can finish.
twoStarDescription: Say it once at a speaking pace and stop if you stumble.
threeStarDescription: If you stumble, mark the sound that caught you.

title: Say what a capo changes
description: Put a capo on one fret and say which open strings moved, without claiming a new key by ear.
oneStarDescription: Put it just behind one fret on all the strings you intend.
twoStarDescription: Sound one open string above the capo.
threeStarDescription: Say the capo moved the open string and that you are not naming the key.

title: See if a letter is under a limit
description: Weigh a letter and say whether it is under a limit you wrote down first.
oneStarDescription: Write the limit before you weigh.
twoStarDescription: Weigh the letter and write the number.
threeStarDescription: Say whether it is under the limit.

title: See if a paper boomerang returns
description: Fold a paper boomerang, throw it once, and say honestly whether it came back.
oneStarDescription: Fold a boomerang shape. Another person can confirm, from what they see or hear, that you can fold the shape.
twoStarDescription: Throw it in an open room.
threeStarDescription: Say whether it returned, and where it landed.

title: See an upside-down view through a pinhole
description: Make a pinhole in a card and describe the upside-down view of a lamp or a window.
oneStarDescription: Prick one small hole in the card, away from your fingers.
twoStarDescription: Look at a lamp or a bright window through a simple pinhole setup and say what is upside down.
threeStarDescription: Say what you cannot tell from that view.

title: Separate ink on paper
description: Put a water-based dot on paper, let water creep through it, and say what colors you see.
oneStarDescription: Put one dot above the water line.
twoStarDescription: Let water climb the paper and stop before the dot runs off the top.
threeStarDescription: Name the colors you see, or say you see only one.

title: Separate two paper rings
description: Make two paper rings that look linked and show whether they are, by the cut you planned.
oneStarDescription: Make two rings in the setup you chose.
twoStarDescription: Pull them and say whether they separate.
threeStarDescription: Show the cut or the slit that decides it.

title: Set a lock to a code you wrote
description: Set a combination lock to a code you wrote down, then open it from the note.
oneStarDescription: Write the code before you scramble the lock.
twoStarDescription: Scramble it and open it using the note.
threeStarDescription: Say where you will keep the note, not on the bag in plain sight if the bag is public.

title: Balance a spoon on your nose
description: Balance a light spoon on your nose for a moment, or say it slid.
oneStarDescription: Place the spoon and let go.
twoStarDescription: Hold still long enough to be seen.
threeStarDescription: Catch it when it slides.

title: Sew a blanket stitch
description: Sew a short blanket stitch along the edge of scrap cloth.
oneStarDescription: Make the first loop on the edge.
twoStarDescription: Sew several stitches that look alike.
threeStarDescription: Point to one loop and say what it holds.

title: Shade a circle so it looks round
description: Shade a circle with one side darker and say where the light is.
oneStarDescription: Say which side the light comes from.
twoStarDescription: Shade the opposite side darker.
threeStarDescription: Ask someone where the light is, from the drawing.

title: Sharpen a pencil to a point
description: Sharpen a pencil until it writes a fine line.
oneStarDescription: Use a sharpener you can hold safely.
twoStarDescription: Write one fine line. Another person can confirm, from what they see or hear, that you can write with the point.
threeStarDescription: Stop before the lead breaks back to a stub, or say it broke and resharpen.

title: Show that touching dice sum to seven
description: Stack two dice and show that the two touching faces add to seven.
oneStarDescription: Stack two dice with faces flat together.
twoStarDescription: Tip them apart and read the two faces that touched.
threeStarDescription: Say the sum, and try a second stack.

title: Skip a stone once
description: Throw a stone so it touches the water more than once, or say the water was wrong for it.
oneStarDescription: Pick a flat stone and say why.
twoStarDescription: Throw it low and say how many touches you saw.
threeStarDescription: Say what you will not claim if you saw only one touch.

title: Snap on both hands
description: Snap the fingers of each hand so another person can hear both snaps.
oneStarDescription: Make one snap a person nearby can hear.
twoStarDescription: Snap the other hand so both snaps were audible.
threeStarDescription: Snap once on each hand when someone points.

title: Solve a rebus
description: Solve a rebus from the pictures and say the phrase.
oneStarDescription: Say what each picture shows.
twoStarDescription: Say the phrase you think they make.
threeStarDescription: Check against the answer or say you have no key.

title: Solve a two-move slider
description: Solve a tiny sliding puzzle that needs only a few moves, and count the moves you used.
oneStarDescription: Say what the goal looks like.
twoStarDescription: Slide until you reach it.
threeStarDescription: Say how many slides you used.

title: Sort buttons by holes
description: Sort a handful of buttons by the number of holes.
oneStarDescription: Label piles for the hole counts you actually see.
twoStarDescription: Put each button in a pile.
threeStarDescription: Put a button aside if the holes are unclear.

title: Sort coins by the year you can read
description: Sort coins into decades or years you can actually read, and set aside worn ones.
oneStarDescription: Read one year aloud. Another person can confirm, from what they see or hear, that you can read a year.
twoStarDescription: Sort the readable coins.
threeStarDescription: Put coins with unreadable years in a separate pile.

title: Sort stones by one feature
description: Sort a few stones by one feature you name before you start.
oneStarDescription: Write the one feature, such as rough or smooth.
twoStarDescription: Sort the stones by that feature only.
threeStarDescription: Point to one stone that could go either way.
